I evaluated it at each by loading the referenced artifact and comparing version integers: d245 (v7), d247 (v8), controlProtocolV2 (2), predecessorV7 (7), predecessorV8 (8), predecessorV9 (9), predecessorV10 (10), predecessorV11 (11) and predecessorV12 (12) are all true. leftoverJoinV13 is the sole false instance, at 13 against 13. findings.whyThisIsABar: The sentence is not decorative. Across this lineage it is the standing device that tells a reader the version token they just read belongs to the cited artifact and not to the speaker. At corpus v12 the collision it denies was hypothetical. At corpus v13 the collision has actually occurred, which is precisely the cycle in which a reader most needs the guidance, and the artifact asserts the opposite of the fact. That is a current-standing clause in a basedOn.*.role contradicted by the bytes of the file it cites, which is the same defect class as the Codex v12 SHOULD-FIX this candidate was dispatched to land, and it sits in the same object graph. It is a bar rather than an advisory because the false statement is load-bearing for exactly the ambiguity the dispatch singled out for a sweep, and because a later D-000 recording would freeze it.
findings.notTheSameAsFailsIf14: failsIf[14] bars a basedOn.*.role, whatIsNotAuthored or failsIf clause that 'uses a bare version token that collides with this artifact's version integer'. Literally read, that tripwire is not tripped: the role writes 'g21 leftover-join.v13' fully qualified throughout, and no bare token stands anywhere in the document. The defect is the inverse shape. The artifact does not commit the collision, it denies that the collision exists. The candidate's own guard set does not cover this, which is why it survived to Stage A.
findings.repair: In basedOn.leftoverJoinV13.role, drop the trailing "Not this artifact's version number." and replace it with a sentence that states the collision plainly, for example: 'g21 leftover-join.v13 shares the version integer 13 with g21-fixture-corpus.v13; the two are different lineages and the shared integer carries no relation.' Consider widening failsIf[14] in the same edit to bar a current-standing clause that denies a version-integer collision which in fact holds, so the guard covers both directions. No fixture byte, digest, count or authority claim changes; this is prose in one node.
